samples.summary: New block validator still doesn't cover the slides arm of the same endpoint, so the guarantee it advertises is partial
samples.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` now walks body blocks, header/footer blocks and table-cell blocks through `assertValidBlock` (alignment allowlist, finite geometry, inline shape). The same controller's slides arm (`assertValidSlide` / `assertValidElement`, lines ~461-519) never validates `element.textBody.blocks`, even though slide text bodies are docs `Block`s persisted verbatim and read back by `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts` (`ALGN`, `listLevelAttr`). The change's own lessons file records exactly this failure mode: "a validator that walks only one of the writer's inputs is worse than none, because it reads as coverage" (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:70-73). Either extend the walker to slide text bodies or drop the API-side allowlist and rely on the sinks.

samples.summary: Yorkie Tree wire format changed (block style attributes now optional/omitted) with no design-doc update
samples.evidence: Both codecs (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts` and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`) now omit absent block-style attributes and ignore non-finite ones on read — a change to the persisted CRDT schema and its read/write contract. docs-collaboration.md still documents `<block ... alignment="left" lineHeight="1.5">` with "Attributes carry `id`, `type`, and block-level style properties", i.e. always-present attributes, and says nothing about the new omit/default-on-read rule. The diff updated docs-docx-import-export.md, docs-tables.md and slides-pptx-export.md but not the doc that owns this schema.

samples.summary: PUT /content validation contract (new 400s: alignment allowlist, inline shape, header/footer walk) is not recorded in the API design doc
samples.evidence: rest-api.md §5.4 describes `PUT .../content` as "replaces the Yorkie root with the body JSON" and documents only the 409 type mismatch. The change makes the endpoint reject payloads it previously accepted (alignment outside left/center/right/justify, non-finite `style.marginTop`, an inline without `style`, a table cell without `style`, a malformed header/footer block, a non-finite `header.marginFromEdge`) — an API contract change for CLI/API-key clients with no doc update anywhere under docs/design/.

samples.summary: Block-style codec hardened by copy-paste in two packages instead of being extracted to the shared @wafflebase/docs model both already depend on
samples.evidence: `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` + `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` are now duplicated verbatim in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts and packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts, with a comment asking future authors to keep them "byte-identical in behavior"; the field list is duplicated a third time in packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts. Both consumers already import @wafflebase/docs (which owns `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE`/`normalizeBlockStyle`), and shared-core-extraction.md names docs-owned/slides-reusing code "the extraction pattern to emulate" (docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:68-70). The change's own lessons file notes the previous round shipped the fix to only one copy — evidence that the manual-sync approach has already failed once.

samples.summary: `HeaderFooter.marginFromEdge` treated as optional on the wire while the model type keeps it required, and docs-header-footer.md still shows it always serialized
samples.evidence: `serializeMarginFromEdge` now omits the attribute and the backend validator accepts `{ header: { blocks: [] } }` without it, but `HeaderFooter` still declares `marginFromEdge: number` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:31-34) and docs/design/docs/docs-header-footer.md:300 documents the serialized node as `{ type: 'header', marginFromEdge: '48' }`. The optional-on-the-wire semantics are recorded only in code comments.

samples.summary: Substantial unrequested scope beyond the issue's outcome/acceptance criterion
samples.evidence: The issue's acceptance criterion is solely "reset the text color → text is uncolored, not the selection color" (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:102-105). The diff additionally adds a backend content-PUT validation layer (alignment allowlist, block geometry, inline shape, header/footer/table-cell walk), rewrites the block-style and marginFromEdge CRDT codecs in two packages, changes PDF export color parsing (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-style-map.ts), and hardens unrelated PPTX attributes (`listLevel` clamping, `ALGN`/underline Map lookups, `<a:lumMod>`/`<a:alpha>` coercion in export/pptx/color.ts). None of these are needed for the acceptance criterion, and several (PDF `rgb()` colors now exporting in color instead of black, previously-accepted PUT payloads now 400) are user-visible behavior changes bundled into a color-reset fix.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` overlaps existing CSS→hex converters elsewhere in the monorepo, and `toDocxHexColor` is a pure alias
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/grids.ts:132 already has `cssColorToHex` (rgb() → #rrggbb for the paste path) and packages/slides/src/import/pptx/color.ts:215 has `normalizeHex`; the new normalizer is a third parser of the same CSS shapes with no note of the others. `toDocxHexColor` in export/docx-style-map.ts adds a name-only indirection over `toRgbHexColor`.

finding.summary: New block validator still doesn't cover the slides arm of the same endpoint, so the guarantee it advertises is partial
finding.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` now walks body blocks, header/footer blocks and table-cell blocks through `assertValidBlock` (alignment allowlist, finite geometry, inline shape). The change's own lessons file records exactly this failure mode: "a validator that walks only one of the writer's inputs is worse than none, because it reads as coverage" (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:70-73). verdict.reason: The absence is literally true — assertValidElement (docs-content.controller.ts:500-520) checks only id/type/frame and no slides block walker exists in packages/backend/src — but the finding is not a blocking design-fit defect. (a) The exact sinks it names as the reason it matters already fail closed on untrusted slide blocks: ALGN is a closed Map with `?? 'l'` (slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:61-74, used at :99) and listLevelAttr coerces/clamps to [0,8], dropping non-numerics (:76-86, used at :100), both with comments naming the content PUT API as the untrusted source. (b) The validator advertises no slides coverage: it is named assertValidDocsBody and assertValidBlockStyle's docstring scopes itself to "body, header, footer and table-cell blocks" and calls itself defence-in-depth with "the exporters clamp at their own sinks" (controller:299-309). (c) The repo's own lessons file that the finding quotes enumerates the required restoration coverage as body/header/footer/table-cell blocks only (lessons:67-73) and states "the sinks are where the guarantee lives" (:63-65). (d) The originating issue's acceptance criteria and non-goals (todo:102-112) say nothing about API-side slides validation, so no acceptance criterion is unmet, nothing is duplicated, no Non-Goal is exceeded, and no design doc is owed. Extra defence-in-depth on the slides arm is a preference (minor), and residual NaN-geometry exposure at the pptx sink would belong to the correctness lens. Also note the finding's evidence misnames the field: `textBody` appears nowhere in the backend or slides model (blocks live at element.data.blocks / data.text.body.blocks, slides/src/model/element.ts:265,297,497).

finding.summary: Block-style codec hardened by copy-paste in two packages instead of being extracted to the shared @wafflebase/docs model both already depend on
finding.evidence: `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` + `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` are now duplicated verbatim in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts and packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts, with a comment asking future authors to keep them "byte-identical in behavior"; the field list is duplicated a third time in packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts. Both consumers already import @wafflebase/docs (which owns `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE`/`normalizeBlockStyle`), and shared-core-extraction.md names docs-owned/slides-reusing code "the extraction pattern to emulate" (docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:68-70). The change's own lessons file notes the previous round shipped the fix to only one copy — evidence that the manual-sync approach has already failed once.

verdict.reason: The duplication exists as described (frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-257, backend docs-tree.ts:139-189, field list again in docs-content.controller.ts:291-297, including the "byte-identical in behavior" comment), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) No existing module is reinvented: @wafflebase/docs owns no Yorkie-Tree attribute codec (its serialize surface is serializeJson/Markdown/Text, packages/docs/src/node.ts:144-149; no Record<string,string> attr codec anywhere in packages/docs/src), and both copies already reuse the model helpers DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE/normalizeBlockStyle they import. So the ask is "create a new shared module," a refactor recommendation, not a reuse/duplication-of-existing-module violation. (b) The frontend/backend mirror is the documented architecture with extraction explicitly deferred: docs-tree.ts:1-22 calls it "a deliberate, narrowly-scoped mirror" because the editor serializer is tied to browser code paths a NestJS process cannot import, and names the future extraction ("If/when this duplication becomes painful, extract a writeDocsRoot() helper into @wafflebase/docs"); docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md:163-168 records the same mirror. The whole codec (inline/cell/border) is mirrored this way, not just block style. (c) The cited evidence misreads the design doc: shared-core-extraction.md:64-70 is the "Already shared, healthy — do not touch" inventory about docs→slides rich-text reuse, not a mandate; that doc's Goals cover OOXML/DrawingML/geometry/canvas triplication across engines, its Non-Goals defer store-level unification (46-48) and its Risks warn against "Over-extraction" (238-240). No stated Non-Goal is exceeded and no Goal requires this extraction. (d) No acceptance criterion is unmet — the issue's criterion is a rendering outcome (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:102-105); extracting a cross-package codec would be unrequested scope. The manual-sync maintenance risk is real but is a "could be cleaner" refactor preference, i.e. minor, which never blocks under this lens.

finding.summary: Block-style serializer is duplicated backend/frontend; only the backend copy was hardened, so the two CRDT encoders now diverge
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` were changed to emit only present/finite fields and to ignore non-finite attributes, but the near-identical copy in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-227 still does `alignment: style.alignment` / `String(style.lineHeight)` unconditionally and `Number(attrs.x)` without a finite check. Both write and read the same Yorkie Tree, so the same document is now encoded/decoded by two different rule sets — the repo's reuse expectation would put this logic in one shared module instead.

verdict.reason: The reviewer's specific quoted evidence does NOT hold: frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:229-257 contains a fully hardened serializeBlockStyle/parseBlockStyle (typeof alignment === 'string' guard, Number.isFinite gates on both write and read) that is behaviorally identical to backend docs-tree.ts:158-189, and its own comment says it is deliberately kept in lockstep. However, the finding's substantive claim — the block/header codec is duplicated backend/frontend and only one copy was hardened, so the same Yorkie Tree attributes are encoded/decoded by two rule sets — is independently verifiable at the same file pair via marginFromEdge: backend has serializeMarginFromEdge/parseMarginFromEdge (docs-tree.ts:318-324, 348+) that omit non-finite values and fall back on read, while the frontend writes String(header.marginFromEdge) unconditionally (yorkie-doc-store.ts:728, 769, 2724) and reads Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48') with no finite check (526, 532). The repo's own lessons doc (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:75-86) names this exact duplication/divergence hazard, including marginFromEdge. Since the duplication-and-divergence defect is real in the working tree, I have no named ground to drop it; low confidence only because the reviewer cited the wrong lines.
